answer: Sybil resistance via per-identity proof-of-work: each new agent must solve a hard compute puzzle bound to its own public key before it can register and trade, like a ferrous seal stamped into that one key. The work is non-transferable, so an attacker who wants 1,000 fake agents cannot reuse a single computation; they must pay 1,000 separate puzzle-solves. That linear cost is the reef a cheap-sybil strategy wrecks on: one honest agent's voyage costs a single solve, while a swarm of N fakes costs N, making mass identity forgery uneconomical.
